bio: Servatius Birkenmayer was born at Munzingen on 4 May 1807 (per his 1836 marriage; his death age, 46 years 11 months 15 days, implies 4 May 1806 — unresolved, 1807 preferred as the tree and marriage agree). His May birth fits the round-1 tip that St. Servatius's feast is 13 May. On 17 Oct 1836 at Munzingen (1836 Act. III): 'Servatius Birkenmayer, lediger Sohn des Johann Birkenmayer, herrschaftl. Waibel[?], und der + Magdalena Erb, nunmehr bürgerlicher Glasermeister, dahier geboren den 4ten May 1807' married 'M[aria] Agatha Heizler, ledige Tochter des + Joseph Heizler, herrschaftlicher Jäger, und der M. Anna Federer von hier, dahier geboren den 26ten Juny 1813'; witnesses Josef Ott, farmer, and Johann Federer, 'formerly glazier, now farmer'; licensed by the Grand-ducal Landamt Freiburg 11 Oct 1836, No. 19140; the 1836 index lists 'I. Birkenmayer Servatius mit Agatha Heizler'. (The FamilySearch index gives the marriage as 27 Oct 1836; the original reading 17 Oct is preferred.) He was a 'Glaser' in 1837, 'Bürger und Glaser' in 1842, and at death 'Schreiner- und Glasermeister u. Bürger' (master joiner/cabinetmaker and glazier). He died 19 Apr 1853 at Munzingen (No. 8), buried 21 Apr, having received the last sacraments; witnesses Friedrich Heizler, gravedigger (his brother-in-law), and Johann Schell, teacher. His toddler Heinrich died about three weeks later. Round 1 and 2 searched for him in vain: Kirchzarten parish database (~30,000 people, ~90 Neuhäuser Birkenmaiers) has no Servatius; GEDBAS and WikiTree have none. Round 2 found an Ancestry index naming Servatius Birkenmayer and 'Agatha Heitzler' as parents of Joseph Birkenmeier (b. 15 Mar 1842 Münzingen, d. Sandusky OH 1904), which led to the Munzingen registers. Nothing ties him to the 1848–49 revolution (he was 41 in 1848). Ancestry tree: 'Servatius Birkenmay… 1807–1853' + 'Maria A Heitzler 1813–1867'.
